712030.t: From Proto-Indo-European *spor-, an o-grade of Proto-Indo-European *sper- (“to strew”). Cognate with σπείρω (speírō, “to sow”), σπέρμα (spérma, “semen, sperm”), and Albanian farë; see σπείρω (speírō) for more.

712089.t: As this word is also Doric and Aeolic, the connection with ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ, “to stand”) must be given up.

712083.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *stegʷʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-eti Proto-Indo-European *stégʷʰeti Proto-Hellenic *stékʷʰō Ancient Greek στέφω (stéphō) Proto-Indo-European *-nós Ancient Greek -νος (-nos) Ancient Greek στέφανος From στέφω (stéphō, “to…

712075.t: From Proto-Indo-European *ster- (“strong; steady”), the same root of Old English starian (“to stare”), Proto-Germanic *staraz (“stiff”), Tocharian B ścīre (“hard; harsh (of words)”).

712087.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *stegʷʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-eti Proto-Indo-European *stégʷʰeti Proto-Hellenic *stékʷʰō Ancient Greek στέφω From Proto-Hellenic *stékʷʰō, from Proto-Indo-European *stégʷʰ-e-ti, from *stegʷʰ- (“to enlace”).

712008.t: From Proto-Hellenic *spérmə, from Proto-Indo-European *spérmn̥, which consists of Proto-Indo-European *sper- + *-mn̥. Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀟𐀗 (pe-mo).

712058.t: From στέγω (stégō, “to cover”) + -νός (-nós), with sense development "covered" > "waterproof, clogged".

712092.t: Uncertain. Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *stl̥-n-eh₂, from *stel- (“to put, place”) (related to στέλλω (stéllō, “to set, arrange”)), with similarities to Old High German stollo.

712059.t: From Proto-Indo-European *(s)teg- (“to cover, roof”). Cognate with Lithuanian sti̇́egiu (“to thatch, to cover a roof”), Latin tegō (“to cover”), Proto-Germanic *þakjaną (“to cover”).

712003.t: García-Ramón suggests that the term is cognate with Vedic Sanskrit पा (pā, “to rise against, be hostile”) and Hittite [script needed] (pippa-, “to overturn”), and reconstructs Proto-Indo-European *(s)peh₂- (“to draw, set in motion”).

712049.t: From Proto-Hellenic *státis, from Proto-Indo-European *stéh₂tis (whence also Latin statiō, Gothic 𐍃𐍄𐌰𐌸𐍃 (staþs, “place”), and Old English stede (English stead)), from *steh₂- (“to stand”).

712052.t: Though traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *stebʰ- (“to be stiff; post”) (compare Sanskrit स्तम्भ (stambha, “pillar”), Old English stæf (“staff”)) via an assumed intermediate sense “stem”, according to Beekes, the word is clearly Pre-Greek,…

712068.t: From an earlier *στενϝός (*stenwós), of unknown further origin, with no known cognates outside Greek. According to Beekes, the suffix of the derivative στενυγρός (stenugrós, “narrow”) suggests Pre-Greek origin.

712040.t: From Proto-Hellenic *statʰmós, from Proto-Indo-European *sth₂-dʰ-mó-s, from *steh₂- (“to stand”).

712035.t: From σπεύδω (speúdō, “to be keen; make haste”) + -η (-ē).

712042.t: According to Beekes, a Proto-Indo-European *th₂eys- (“dough”), whence also Proto-Slavic *těsto (“dough”), Old Irish táis (“dough”), and Old English þǣsma (“leaven”), with an influence from στέαρ (stéar, “fat”).

712006.t: From Proto-Hellenic *spéřřō, from Proto-Indo-European *spéryeti, from *sper- (“to sprinkle, scatter, strew”). The only known secure cognate is Hittite 𒅖𒉺𒀀𒊑 (iš-pa-a-ri /⁠išpāri⁠⁠/, “to spread out, strew”) (< *spor-ey).

712053.t: Traditionally derived from Proto-Indo-European *stn̥gʰ-u-s, from a root *ste(n)gʰ- (“to stick”), and compared with Proto-Germanic *stinganą (“to sting, stick out”), Lithuanian stangùs (“fixed, stiff”), Latvian stingt (“to harden”).

712057.t: From στέγω (stégō, “to cover”) + -η (-ē, action noun suffix).

712011.t: From Proto-Indo-European *spewd- (“to press, hurry”). Cognate with Albanian punë, Lithuanian spáusti, Old Armenian փոյթ (pʻoytʻ).

712037.t: Uncertain, but possibly from στάδιος (stádios, “firm, fixed”), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“to stand”), in reference to the fixed distance of the course.

712027.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *sper- Proto-Indo-European *-yeti Proto-Indo-European *spéryeti Proto-Hellenic *spéřřō Ancient Greek σπείρω (speírō) Proto-Hellenic *-ā́ Ancient Greek -α (-ā) ? Proto-Indo-European *sper- Proto-Indo-European *-h₂…

712054.t: With quantitative metathesis of ῆα (êă) to έα (éā), from Proto-Hellenic *stā́wər, from Proto-Indo-European *stéh₂-wr̥, from *steh₂- (“to stand”). Compare πῖαρ (pîar), οὖθαρ (oûthăr).

712007.t: From Proto-Indo-European *spend-. Cognate to Latin spondeo.

712074.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sterg- (literally “to cover, to protect”). Possibly related to Proto-Slavic *sterťi (“to guard”) and Welsh serch (“love, affection”).

712091.t: Late Hellenistic Koine back-formation from ἕστηκα (héstēkă, “I have stood”), perfect of ἵστημι (hĭ́stēmĭ).

712080.t: From Proto-Indo-European *stér(h₃)-no-m, from Proto-Indo-European *sterh₃- (“to be broad, spread out”). Cognate with Proto-West Germanic *stirniju (“forehead”).

712004.t: From Proto-Indo-European *sper-yeh₂-, from *sper- (“to twist”), and thus cognate with σπάργανον (spárganon, “swaddling clothes”), σπάρτον (spárton, “rope, cable”), and σπεῖρον (speîron, “shroud”).

712046.t: From Proto-Indo-European *stéh₂mn̥ (“that which stands, stature”). Cognate with Latin stāmen (“warp of a loom; thread hanging from a distaff”).

712095.t: From Proto-Indo-European *stéh₂mn̥ (“that which stands, stature”). Cognate with Latin stāmen and Ancient Greek στάμνος (stámnos, “jar”).

712022.t: Uncertain: * Furnée connects ἄσβολος (ásbolos, “soot”) and σπολεύς (spoleús, “loaf”), the former with a prothetic vowel α- (a-), and both showing a variation δ ~ λ (d ~ l).

712036.t: From στάξ (stắx, “drop”) + -ών (-ṓn), of uncertain origin; also found in στάζω (stắzō, “to drop; to drip”).

712013.t: The formation is similar to παλάμη (palámē, “palm of the hand”), δόχμη (dókhmē, “breadth of the hand”) and πυγμή (pugmḗ, “distance between the elbow and the knuckles”). According to Beekes, it's probably from Pre-Greek.

712038.t: From στάξ (stắx, “drop”) + *-ϳω (*-jō), of uncertain origin; also found in σταγών (stăgṓn, “drop”).

712099.t: From the root of στείβω (steíbō, “to tread on, stamp on”).

712015.t: The formation is similar to ἀστήρ (ăstḗr, “star”) and αἰθήρ (aithḗr, “ether”).

712098.t: Likely from Proto-Indo-European *sterh₁- (“stiff, fixed, infertile”) and related to στερεός (stereós, “stiff, hard”), though the morphological details are unclear.

712072.t: From Proto-Hellenic *sténō, from Proto-Indo-European *(s)tenh₂- (“to thunder”), compare Sanskrit स्तनति (stanati, “to drone, thunder”), Proto-Germanic *stenaną (“to moan, groan”), Proto-Slavic *stenàti (“to groan, to moan”).

712012.t: From the same Pre-Greek source as σπέος (spéos) and σπῆλυγξ (spêlŭnx).

712066.t: From στένω (sténō, “to moan, lament”) + -άζω (-ázō, frequentative suffix).

712002.t: Of unclear origin, though the word's ending -άλη (-ắlē) and semantics are reminiscent of those of κραιπάλη (kraipắlē, “bout of drinking”), δαιταλεύς (daităleús, “banqueter”).
